skills.name: Prepare sulphur dioxide in the laboratory and state its physical properties

note.text:
Laboratory preparation: a sulphite and a dilute acid.
Na2SO3 + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H2O + SO2
The acid is added to sodium sulphite in a flask; the gas is dried by passing it through concentrated sulphuric acid, and collected by downward delivery into a dry gas jar, because it is denser than air and very soluble in water.
Sulphur dioxide can also be made by burning sulphur in air, or by heating copper with concentrated sulphuric acid.
Physical properties: a colourless, poisonous gas with a sharp choking smell; denser than air (relative molecular mass 64); very soluble in water, giving an acidic solution; easily liquefied. It must be made in a fume cupboard.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to write the equation for preparing sulphur dioxide, explain how it is dried and collected, and state its physical properties.
Builds on: Lesson {2} (sulphur burns to {formula('SO2')}) and Form Three gas collection.
Leads to: Lesson {4} (the chemical properties of {formula('SO2')}) and the Contact process.

sections.heading: Preparation
sections.text:
In the laboratory, sulphur dioxide is made from a sulphite and a dilute acid:
{formula('Na2SO3')} + {2}{formula('HCl')} → {2}{formula('NaCl')} + {formula('H2O')} + {formula('SO2')}
The dilute acid is run onto sodium sulphite in a flask. The gas is led through a wash bottle of concentrated sulphuric acid, which dries it without reacting, and then down into a dry gas jar.
It can also be made by burning sulphur in air, or by heating copper with concentrated sulphuric acid:
Cu + {2}{formula('H2SO4')} → {formula('CuSO4')} + {formula('SO2')} + {2}{formula('H2O')}.

sections.heading: Physical properties and collection
sections.text:
Sulphur dioxide is a colourless gas with a sharp choking smell. It is poisonous, so it must be prepared in a fume cupboard.
Its relative molecular mass is {32} + {2} × {16} = {64}, well above the average for air, so it is denser than air.
It is very soluble in water, giving an acidic solution of sulphurous acid.
Being dense and very soluble, it is collected by downward delivery into a dry gas jar: not over water, which would dissolve it.
It is easily turned to a liquid by pressure, which is how it is stored and transported.

key_words.meaning: a salt containing the {formula('SO3')} ion with a {2}− charge, such as {formula('Na2SO3')}
collecting a dense gas by leading it to the bottom of a jar
a substance that removes water from a gas without reacting with it
a cabinet that draws harmful fumes away

mistake.right: it is collected by downward delivery
mistake.why: {formula('SO2')} is very soluble in water, so collecting it over water would lose the gas.

worked_example.problem: Write the equation for the laboratory preparation of sulphur dioxide from sodium sulphite and dilute hydrochloric acid, and name the drying agent.
steps: A sulphite and a dilute acid give a salt, water and sulphur dioxide.
Sulphur dioxide is an acidic gas, so it is dried with concentrated sulphuric acid, which does not react with it.

cards.idea: A sulphite with a dilute acid gives sulphur dioxide.

cards.idea: An acidic gas is dried with concentrated sulphuric acid, never with a base.

pick.q: Why is quicklime, {formula('CaO')}, not used to dry sulphur dioxide?
pick.r: Quicklime is basic and reacts with the acidic gas
w: Quicklime is not a drying agent at all
Quicklime would make the gas wetter
Quicklime dissolves the gas in water
e: Quicklime IS a drying agent; it is used for ammonia. The problem here is that it reacts.
A drying agent removes water; quicklime does not add any.
Quicklime reacts with the gas; it does not dissolve it in water.
pick.y: An acidic gas must be dried with an acidic drying agent, such as concentrated sulphuric acid.

pick.q: Which drying agent is used for ammonia, and why?
pick.r: Quicklime, because ammonia is alkaline and would react with an acidic drying agent
w: Concentrated sulphuric acid, because it dries every gas
Water, because ammonia dissolves in it
No drying agent can be used with ammonia
e: Concentrated sulphuric acid reacts with ammonia to give ammonium sulphate.
Water dissolves ammonia instead of drying it.
Quicklime dries it well.
pick.y: A drying agent must not react with the gas: a basic gas needs a basic drying agent.

pick.q: A gas is passed through a wash bottle of concentrated sulphuric acid. What is this for?
pick.r: To remove water vapour from the gas
w: To cool the gas
To make the gas more soluble
To change the gas into an acid
e: Cooling is not the purpose, and the acid does not cool the gas.
Drying does not change how soluble the gas is.
The acid does not react with a gas it is used to dry.
pick.y: Concentrated sulphuric acid takes up water strongly, which is why it is a drying agent.

pick.q: Why must the gas jar be dry when sulphur dioxide is collected?
pick.r: The gas is very soluble, so any water in the jar would dissolve some of it
w: Water would make the gas explode
A wet jar would crack
Water would turn the gas brown
e: Sulphur dioxide does not explode with water; it dissolves.
The jar does not crack; the problem is loss of the gas.
Sulphur dioxide stays colourless in water; it forms sulphurous acid.
pick.y: {formula('SO2')} is very soluble in water, so a wet jar would hold less gas.

pick.q: Which reagents are used to prepare sulphur dioxide in the laboratory?
pick.r: Sodium sulphite and dilute hydrochloric acid
w: Sodium sulphate and dilute hydrochloric acid
Sodium sulphide and dilute hydrochloric acid
Sodium carbonate and dilute hydrochloric acid
e: A sulphate does not give off {formula('SO2')} with a dilute acid; a sulphite does.
A sulphide gives hydrogen sulphide, {formula('H2S')}, not {formula('SO2')}.
A carbonate gives carbon dioxide.

pick.r: By downward delivery, because it is denser than air
w: By downward displacement of water
Over water
By upward delivery, because it is less dense than air
e: {formula('SO2')} is very soluble in water, so it cannot be collected over or through water.
It would dissolve in the water.
Its relative molecular mass is {64}, well above the average for air, so it is denser.
pick.y: A dense, very soluble gas is collected by downward delivery into a dry gas jar.

pick.q: Which drying agent is used for sulphur dioxide?
w: Quicklime, {formula('CaO')}
Sodium hydroxide pellets
Water
e: Quicklime is basic and would react with the acidic gas.
Sodium hydroxide is a base and would absorb the gas.
Water dissolves the gas instead of drying it.
pick.y: An acidic gas is dried with concentrated sulphuric acid, which does not react with it.

pick.q: What is the smell and colour of sulphur dioxide?
pick.r: Colourless, with a sharp choking smell
w: Brown, with a choking smell
Colourless, with a smell of rotten eggs
Yellow and odourless
e: Brown is the colour of nitrogen dioxide.
Rotten eggs is the smell of hydrogen sulphide.
Sulphur dioxide is colourless and certainly not odourless.
pick.y: {formula('SO2')} is a colourless, poisonous gas with a sharp choking smell.

pick.q: Why must sulphur dioxide be prepared in a fume cupboard?
pick.r: It is poisonous and irritates the eyes and lungs
w: It catches fire easily
It explodes on contact with air
It is only a nuisance because of its colour
e: Sulphur dioxide does not burn; it is itself a product of burning.
It does not explode in air.
The gas is colourless; the danger is that it is poisonous.
pick.y: Breathing it in damages the lungs, so it must be used where the fumes can be drawn away.

questions.prompt: Find the relative molecular mass of {formula(F)}.

misconceptions.explain: {totalAtoms(F)} is the NUMBER of atoms; the mass adds their relative atomic masses.
Count the mass of every atom, not the number of different elements.

solution: Add the relative atomic mass of every atom in the formula.

pick.q: Put the steps of preparing a dry jar of sulphur dioxide in order.
s: Place sodium sulphite in the flask and set up the apparatus in a fume cupboard
Add dilute hydrochloric acid from the thistle funnel
Pass the gas given off through concentrated sulphuric acid to dry it
Lead the dry gas to the bottom of a dry gas jar by downward delivery
Cover the full jar with a greased glass plate

pick.q: Put the path of the gas through the apparatus in order, from where it is made.
s: The gas is given off in the reaction flask
It passes along the delivery tube
It bubbles through the concentrated sulphuric acid in the wash bottle
It leaves the wash bottle dry
It sinks to the bottom of the gas jar

pick.q: Put the steps of testing a jar of sulphur dioxide in order.
s: Lift the glass plate a little and smell the gas carefully by wafting
Lower in a piece of damp blue litmus paper
Note that the litmus turns red
Note that the red colour is then bleached away
